clue.text: Calm businessman on river, not for all to see

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative, a travelling businessman

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the next item from the river's name

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in Yorkshire (and another in Sussex)
U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all audiences

explanation.surface: A businessman relaxing on a river, somewhere private away from prying eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for all to see' is the British U film certificate, suitable for all audiences; 'not' takes it out of the river's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Repose is rest or tranquillity, a synonym for calm as a noun.

clue.text: Greed shown by king with potential to lose head

parts.note: R is short for Rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: losing its head means the word for potential drops its opening letter

parts.note: capacity is potential, the ability to do something

explanation.surface: A grasping monarch whose ambitions might cost him his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like the king's head, but 'to lose head' just drops the first letter of the word for potential.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapacity is aggressive, grasping avarice, a direct synonym for greed.

clue.text: English poet, vain creature

definitions.meaning: Thomas Love P., the satirical poet and novelist who wrote Nightmare Abbey and was Shelley's friend
the male peafowl, which struts and fans its tail and is a byword for vanity

explanation.surface: An English poet dismissed as a conceited, preening type.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird shares its name with the poet Thomas Love Peacock, and the bird's display makes it proverbially vain.

clue.text: Two directions misinterpreted in a wood and mountainous area

parts.note: south, one compass direction, is S
north, the second compass direction, is N

indicators.note: misinterpreted means the following words are read wrongly, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone gets lost after misreading directions in a forest in hill country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misinterpreted' seems to govern the directions, but it scrambles the three words that follow; the two directions are south and north, kept as they are.
explanation.definitionFit: Snowdonia is the mountainous national park in north Wales around Snowdon, Wales's highest peak.

clue.text: Trusted figure reformed law in beginning

indicators.note: in tells us the rearranged word sits inside the word for beginning

parts.note: a start is a beginning

indicators.note: reformed means remade in a new shape, so the letters of law are rearranged

explanation.surface: A reliable public figure who started out by overhauling the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' turns LAW into ALW, which goes 'in' START.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalwart is a loyal, dependable supporter, someone who can be trusted.

clue.text: Master of form at Cheltenham, maybe?

definitions.text: Master of form at Cheltenham, maybe?

parts.words: Master of form at Cheltenham, maybe?
parts.note: reads like a schoolmaster at Cheltenham College, but means a bookmaker who studies racehorses' form at Cheltenham racecourse

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher in charge of a class at a public school in Cheltenham.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheltenham is both a public school and Britain's leading jump-racing course; 'form' is a school class or a horse's racing record.
explanation.definitionFit: A turf accountant is a jokey formal term for a bookmaker, who must know horses' form at racecourses like Cheltenham.

clue.text: Before noon, everyone gets up to see animal

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards, reversing them

parts.note: a.m. means before noon
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everyone rises early in the morning to go and see an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: AM followed by ALL is AMALL; 'gets up' reverses it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The llama is a South American domesticated camelid, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Rising member of academy, one in stylish old hat?

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the letters read upwards, so they are reversed

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

indicators.note: in places the letter for one inside the word for stylish

parts.note: chic means stylish
A is one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: An academician on the up, sporting a smart but dated hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' works only because this is a down entry; 'old hat' is the definition, not part of the picture of the stylish hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Old hat is an idiom for outdated or old-fashioned, matching archaic.

clue.text: Two notes on an artist

indicators.note: two tells us the note is given twice in a row

parts.note: ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
taken as written

explanation.surface: A couple of notes written about a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian was the great Venetian Renaissance painter, an example of an artist.

clue.text: Preppiest chain devised training scheme

indicators.note: devised means worked out or made up, so these letters are formed into something new

explanation.surface: A chain of very preppy shops dreams up a staff training programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devised' rearranges PREPPIEST and CHAIN together.
explanation.definitionFit: An apprenticeship is a period of on-the-job instruction in a trade, a structured training programme.

clue.text: Close to camp, European's moving clear of northern fog

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so we take the final letter of camp
moving means the remaining letters shift into a new order
clear of means the letter for northern is removed

parts.note: the word European, its possessive 's read as a further letter
the 's of the possessive supplies an S

explanation.surface: A European heads south from a camp to escape the northern fog.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's counts as a letter here; 'clear of' removes the N, and 'moving' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A pea-souper is a thick yellowish fog, as in old London smogs.

clue.text: Government agency backed religious books in course

indicators.note: backed means the agency's letters are read backwards

parts.note: the CSA was the Child Support Agency, a UK government agency
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of religious books

explanation.surface: A government body backs religious texts being taught on a course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns CSA into ASC; the definition is a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is the famous racecourse in Berkshire, home of Royal Ascot.

clue.text: Food before wine recalled as stew

parts.note: chow is slang for food

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters of the wine are read in reverse

parts.note: red is red wine

explanation.surface: Remembering a meal that came before the wine as a stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' looks like remembering, but means the wine is called back, read in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Chowder is a thick soupy seafood stew, so it can stand for a stew.

clue.text: A scientific establishment attended by a scholar in state

parts.note: a lab, short for laboratory, is a scientific establishment
MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate scholar

explanation.surface: A research laboratory with a visiting academic somewhere in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabama is one of the southern states of the USA.

clue.text: Sign with ex-London Mayor as recipient?

parts.note: to marks the recipient of something, as in a gift label
Ken Livingstone was the first Mayor of London

explanation.surface: A gift tag addressed to a former Mayor of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Livingstone was London's first elected Mayor (2000-2008).
explanation.definitionFit: A token is a symbol or sign of something, as in a token of affection.

clue.text: Kiss doctor in ornamental accessory

parts.note: to neck is to kiss and cuddle
to doctor a drink is to lace it with something

explanation.surface: A doctor is kissed by someone wearing a decorative piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' is a verb here: tamper with or spike.
explanation.definitionFit: A necklace is a decorative chain worn round the neck, a piece of jewellery.

clue.text: Take on ex-Foreign Secretary, showing tipping point in exasperation?

parts.note: to last is to keep on or carry on, the sense of taking on in go on, endure
Jack Straw was British Foreign Secretary from 2001 to 2006

explanation.surface: Taking on a former Foreign Secretary pushes someone beyond their patience.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Straw was UK Foreign Secretary under Tony Blair.
explanation.definitionFit: The last straw is the final small annoyance that breaks someone's patience, from the straw that broke the camel's back.

clue.text: Fabric entirely altered I put out on back of settee

indicators.note: altered means changed, so the remaining letters are rearranged
put out means the I is removed from the word before the letters are rearranged
the back of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone completely changes the upholstery, putting a cloth on the back of the sofa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' drops I from ENTIRELY; 'altered' rearranges ENTRELY into TERYLEN, then 'back of' adds E.
explanation.definitionFit: Terylene is a British trade name for polyester fibre, a synthetic fabric.

clue.text: Concoction of rum? It is a dessert

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so the following letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Asks whether a rum-laced mixture counts as a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concoction of' rearranges RUM, IT IS and A together.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiramisu is an Italian dessert of coffee-soaked sponge and mascarpone, often laced with liqueur.

clue.text: A lot of abuse linked to popular hormone

indicators.note: a lot of, but not all, means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: an insult is verbal abuse
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: Plenty of abuse is tied to a hormone that is in fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' trims INSULT to INSUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulin is the pancreatic hormone that regulates blood sugar.

clue.text: Frugal items parent is keeping

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the answer is held inside the words items parent

explanation.surface: A parent holding on to things out of thrift.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits in itemS PAREnt.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare can mean meagre or economical, as in a spare diet, so it fits frugal.

clue.text: Con — a party's aim in election on street

parts.note: a party contesting an election aims to gain seats

explanation.surface: A con trick: a political party's election ambitions out on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Con' is not a trick or a Conservative here: it is as in pros and cons.
explanation.definitionFit: Con, as in pros and cons, means an argument opposed, so it equals the preposition meaning opposed to.

clue.text: Part of game? It's relayed by bookies with parts swapped

indicators.note: the two halves of the signalling term change places

parts.note: tic-tac is the hand-signalling system bookmakers use to pass on odds at racecourses

explanation.surface: A move in a game that bookmakers pass along to each other.
explanation.walkthrough: TIC-TAC is the British racecourse bookies' sign language; swapping TIC and TAC gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic is a planned manoeuvre, part of a team's or player's game plan.

clue.text: A book with instruction for crossworders is free

parts.note: a crossword's task for its solvers is to solve it

explanation.surface: A book of crosswords comes without charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve is to free someone from guilt or obligation, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Sudden move in winter sports event around November

indicators.note: around means the sled event's letters go round the letter for November

parts.note: the luge is a winter sports event, sliding feet-first on a small sled
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A sudden movement during a winter sports race in late autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps LUGE round N.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunge is a sudden forward thrust of the body, as in fencing.

clue.text: Cuts damaged a US city and foreign region

indicators.note: damaged means broken up, so the letters of cuts are rearranged

parts.note: NY is New York, a US city

explanation.surface: Spending cuts have hurt a US city and a region abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges only Cuts; 'foreign' is fair because the setter writes from Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuscany is a region of central Italy, foreign from a British setter's viewpoint.

clue.text: See in leather a hooked feature

indicators.note: in places the word for see inside the word for leather

parts.note: tan can mean leather, from tanning hides
lo is an old word meaning see or behold

explanation.surface: Look closely at a leather item and you find a hooked part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is not a verb of looking but the archaic interjection lo, as in lo and behold.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is a bird of prey's curved claw, a hooked part of its foot.

clue.text: Obstacle in much of language recited initially by a new church

indicators.note: much of means most, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: Hindi is a major language of India

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of recited

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A recitation in a foreign tongue is a barrier for a new congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'much of' cuts HINDI to HIND.
explanation.definitionFit: A hindrance is something that gets in the way, a synonym for an obstacle.

clue.text: Right-winger with allure creating offence

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, a right-wing politician
to tempt is to allure or entice

explanation.surface: A right-wing politician's charm causes offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt can be an offence, as in contempt of court, the crime of defying a court.

clue.text: Change limited article for bandage

indicators.note: limited means cut short, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: to swap is to change or exchange
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Swap a restrictive item for a dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited' trims SWAP to SWA.
explanation.definitionFit: To swathe is to wrap or bind in strips of cloth, as one does with a bandage.
